title: First-contact onboarding: manifest-driven conversion + deterministic canary smoke
creator: Marisol Chen
description:
Objective: Implement a lightweight 'first-contact' onboarding pipeline for community-supplied LLM weights that produces a deterministic conversion manifest, a reproducible pinned artifact, and an automated canary smoke validation report. Scope includes weights intake, reproducible conversion to runtime format, generation of a signed conversion manifest for pinning, and a small deterministic smoke test suite that verifies runtime readiness and basic perf/quality metrics.

Out of scope: full-scale stress benchmarking, exhaustive safety evals, or manual curation workflows; those will be handled by follow-up tickets.

High-level design:
- Intake: accept a signed weight bundle (tar/manifest) through the existing asset-gateway endpoint. Basic provenance checks and virus-signature scan are performed.
- Manifest generation: run deterministic conversion using pinned converter image; record exact converter commit, quantization flags, tokenizer hash, sequence-length assumptions, and a KV-cache compatibility fingerprint. Output is an immutable YAML manifest that can be uploaded to the model catalog and used for pin creation.
- Conversion: conversion runs in a reproducible container (deterministic env + cached wheel set). The conversion pipeline writes content-addressable artifacts and emits a canonical tokenization sample.
- Canary smoke: lightweight suite (10 prompts, 3 sequence lengths) executed against the converted artifact in a staging runtime with KV-enabled and KV-disabled modes. Collect latency percentiles, token-accuracy (checksum on deterministic prompts), and a small output-similarity metric against the reference tokenization sample.
- Pinning: when smoke passes guardrails, auto-create a candidate pin with a human review step in console. Pin includes manifest URI, conversion commit, benchmark snapshot, and suggested variant tags.
- Telemetry: emit events for intake-start, convert-start, convert-complete, smoke-start, smoke-result, pin-created. Include artifacts and links in telemetry for replay.

Acceptance criteria:
- For a given public checkpoint, the pipeline produces the same conversion manifest on repeated runs (byte-for-byte manifest match).
- Canary smoke runs deterministically on the same converted artifact and passes defined thresholds (latency p95 < configured SLO, token-checksum match).
- Generated manifest is uploaded to the catalog and visible in the Console with links to artifacts and smoke report.
- Human review flow can accept/reject a pin via Console and marks final pin metadata.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Determinism requires strong environment pinning (containers + wheels). This increases maintenance burden for converter images.
- Tight determinism can reject acceptable community weights that embed non-deterministic ops or metadata; fallback policy will capture conversion failures and route to manual curation.
- Canary smoke is intentionally small to remain fast; it may miss subtle regressions. We will tie the small suite to automatic suggestion for expanded smoke if change is large.

Rollout plan: feature-flag the manifest and canary path behind 'first_contact_onboard_v2'. Start by enabling for internal OSS corpus only, then open to external once 3 internal-week reliability windows pass.

Operational runbook links and artifacts: see attachments. The PR contains a converter image tag and unit tests covering manifest reproducibility.
